why: Dropping from three players to two while Teams is selected LEAVES the pane in Teams -- a mode it no longer offers. The disabled button cannot prevent this state, because the player never touches the mode row to reach it; they touch the player count. The result is a pane whose mode control shows a refused option as chosen, whose Teams-only friendly-fire row is still on screen, and whose Start may be refused by the one-team gate with no visible way to fix it, since the team controls are the thing that would let a player split the sides. Exactly ONE test fails, which is the point of the entry: the offer rule and this consistency rule are separate claims, and a build could satisfy the first while breaking the second -- the disabled button and the forced fallback are not the same guarantee. Scoped to hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
